questions.stem: Which option correctly describes a stimulus?

options.text: Any detectable change in the surroundings
options.explanation: A stimulus is a change that can be detected by an organism.
That describes a receptor, not the stimulus.
That describes the response.
Stimuli are changes; constant conditions stimulate nothing.

questions.stem: Where are receptors found in humans?

options.explanation: That is a plant context, not a human one.
Human receptors are located in sense organs.
Bones support the body; they are not the receptor sites named here.
Receptors are not limited to one organ.

questions.stem: How do plants detect stimuli such as light or gravity?

options.explanation: Plant responses to light and gravity prove detection happens.
Detection is not restricted to flowers.

options.text: With specialised cells sensitive to light, gravity or water
options.explanation: Plants use specialised cells rather than sense organs.
Plants have no eyes.

questions.stem: Which list gives the response types named in this note?

options.explanation: That is development, not a response category here.
Movement is one category among three.
Mutations are not responses to stimuli in this sense.

options.text: Moving toward or away, secreting chemicals, adjusting body processes
options.explanation: Those are the three named response categories.

questions.stem: Why do organisms bother responding to stimuli at all?

options.text: To raise their chance of survival
options.explanation: Responses improve survival — escaping predators, finding food, keeping conditions stable.
Responses conserve life, not waste energy deliberately.
Size increase is not the stated purpose.
Mating display is not the purpose named here.

questions.stem: Define a stimulus in one sentence.
questions.modelAnswer: A detectable change in the environment, such as light, temperature, sound, chemicals or touch.

questions.stem: Name the structures that detect stimuli in humans and in plants.
questions.modelAnswer: Humans use receptors in sense organs; plants use specialised cells.

questions.stem: Explain why detection alone is not enough for survival.
questions.modelAnswer: Detecting a change does nothing by itself; the organism must also produce a response — moving away, secreting chemicals or adjusting processes — because it is the response that raises the chance of surviving, whether by escaping a predator, finding food or keeping internal conditions steady.

questions.stem: A rabbit hears a fox nearby. Identify the stimulus and give one response that would improve the rabbit's survival.
questions.modelAnswer: The stimulus is the sound of the fox; the rabbit's receptors detect it and a life-saving response would be moving away from the sound — running to cover — which raises its chance of escaping the predator.
